game: DET @ CIN | 2025-10-05 16:25 ET | CIN +10.5 / DET -10.5 | total 49.5 | outdoors, weather forecast not saved

script.base: Detroit is a 10.5-point favorite with a 30.0 implied total against Cincinnati's 19.5, so DET should lead by the second half and close by running. Gibbs (49 carries, 252 yards, 5.14 YPC over weeks 2-4) is the lead back ahead of Montgomery (32/220) into a CIN run defense allowing 4.67 YPC. Cincinnati, trailing, leaks off the run — Brown is at 90 yards on 36 carries (2.5 YPC) in that window — and throws toward Chase (30 targets, 238 yards). The 49.5 total adds plays, but the split is DET-skewed, not a shootout.
script.flip1: Blowout: DET is up big by halftime, Gibbs and Montgomery bank early rush yards, then starter snaps get cut, and Goff, St. Brown and Williams stall. CIN garbage-time throws pad Chase, Higgins and Fant while Brown never gets a rushing rhythm.
script.flip2: Competitive: CIN hangs within a score, DET cannot grind late, Goff stays in the pass game (St. Brown's 26 targets / 262 yards stay live), and Brown keeps about a 12-carry role so a rush under dies. A Decker inactive (Doubtful, shoulder) can sit inside either flip and turn DET's run efficiency down without changing the favorite.

matchup.shell: No coverage charting in the pack, so MOFO/MOFC and man/zone are unknown. Known rates: CIN blitzes 21%, DET blitzes 44%. DET EPA/dropback is 0.96 vs blitz and only 0.11 vs no blitz, so Cincinnati's low-blitz shell is the look Detroit's passing game has been worse against. CIN EPA/dropback is -0.08 vs blitz and -0.46 vs no blitz, so Detroit's blitz is the less-bad world for Cincinnati and both are negative.
matchup.pressure: CIN will not manufacture the pressure DET has feasted on (21% blitz). The live pressure story is Decker Doubtful: a backup left tackle can create heat without a blitz, which cuts deep WR yards and lifts RB/TE quick catches. DET's 44% blitz is what CIN's QB has to answer; Cincinnati is negative EPA either way (-0.08 when blitzed).
matchup.bleeds: CIN allows 4.67 YPC and 12 runs of 10+, plus 14 passes of 20+ for 159 yards. YPA: left 7.4 (60 att), middle 6.1 (29), right 7.31 (64) — they bleed the run and the outside, and are relatively sound in the middle. DET allows 3.94 YPC and 12 runs of 10+, plus 13 passes of 20+ for 132. YPA: left 7.63 (43), middle 10.89 (28), right 5.55 (47) — DET bleeds the middle, is stingy to the right and vs the run, with McNeill Out as a caveat on that run number.
matchup.overlap: The clean overlap is Detroit's run game into Cincinnati's 4.67 YPC front, with Stewart Out: Gibbs (5.14 YPC, about 16 carries a game L3) attacks the soft spot. St. Brown (26 targets) is more likely to see CIN's best zone (middle 6.1 YPA) than the weak outside — no charting to confirm. Williams (403 air yards on 15 targets) overlaps CIN's explosive/outside leak, but Decker Doubtful cuts against that. Cincinnati's overlap is the middle, where DET allows 10.89 YPA: Chase (30 targets, 188 air) plus Fant/Gesicki/Brown checkdowns, helped by Cunningham Out and by Joseph only if he sits. Higgins's 223 air yards on 16 targets overlap the deep game DET's 44% blitz tends to kill.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Decker sat, the left side caved, and Gibbs was hit in the backfield — something like 14 carries for the low 60s, the same miss as his 67-yard game — while Montgomery closed after DET went up big and Gibbs was done for the night. On the other side McNeill's absence was the story: CIN stayed within 10 into the fourth, never fully abandoned the run, and Brown turned a 12-carry role into the mid-40s or low-50s, which is what 43, 47 and 40 already said his non-fluke games look like. The four-game medians (Gibbs 79, Brown 41.5) were the market, and the card over-fit a committee back plus a grinder whose one 3-yard game created the 30-yard mean. No no-vig was ever available to prove either number was off.
slip_story: One story only: DET -10.5 controls and runs, CIN +10.5 falls behind and cannot run. Gibbs rush over is the favorite clock-killing stack; Brown rush under is the dog-abandons-the-run stack. They win together. Do not add St. Brown or Williams overs (those need DET to keep throwing), Chase over (spike plus a volume edge in a yards market), or a total under with these same-game rush leans. No TDs, no receptions, one market per player, two legs.
